problem: Most VLN agents follow an 'observe-and-reason' schema, reacting to the immediate view and static instructions without modeling what lies beyond it, which hurts long-horizon navigation. Prior imagination methods (Pathdreamer, PanoGen) generate offline and treat imagined content as auxiliary rather than as part of decision-making.
motivation: Humans imagine the goal (e.g. a kitchen) and its layout before acting. The paper argues that explicit, online goal imagination, grounded against the current observation and fed into interpretable reasoning, helps with observation limits and the vision-language modality gap on long paths.
key_idea: An 'imagine-and-align' loop: a diffusion model imagines the next goal scene, a Perceptual Alignment Filter grounds it in the current view as an attention map, and a fine-tuned LLM does chain-of-thought action selection over it.
insight: The ablation on R2R val-unseen shows imagination matters most: removing it drops SR from 77.8 to 66.7 and raises NE from 2.92 to 3.98. Removing the filter drops SR to 68.3, removing AIS to 73.4, and removing CoT to 71.5 (mainly hurting SPL and path efficiency). The text also claims imagination gives +11.1% SR on long paths (>15m) on RoboTHOR, but that result is shown only in a figure or in the text, without a table.
method: Adaptive Imagination Scheduler (AIS): switches between static (instruction-entity) and dynamic (history plus observation) goal prediction. It uses static mode only when trajectory uncertainty u_t (action entropy, path deviation) is below a threshold and the cosine similarity s_t between imagined and observed image embeddings is above a threshold; the thresholds are hand-tuned.

Visual Imagination Module: Qwen2-VL captions a candidate scene, and a LoRA-finetuned Stable Diffusion v1.5 synthesizes the imagined image I_SD. An inpainted version I_inpaint of the current observation is also created using the same caption.

Perceptual Alignment Filter (PAF): a shared ResNet-18 encodes O_t, I_SD and I_inpaint; multi-head attention fuses them and a decoder outputs a spatial attention map A_t. It is trained with BCE plus soft Dice loss on 30k quadruples, with pseudo-GT masks from Grounded-SAM on Qwen caption entities.

Navigational CoT decision: LLaMA2-7B with LoRA outputs a three-stage reasoning trace (goal grounding, perceptual verification, decision justification) and the action. Inputs are the instruction, observation captions, a textual summary of the attention map, and history.
R2R-Imagine dataset: over 250k imagined 256x256 images across R2R splits, at ~4.2 s per image on an A100; the LoRA is trained on 5k goal-caption pairs from MP3D.

setting.backbone: Stable Diffusion v1.5 (LoRA-finetuned) + Qwen2-VL (captioning) + ResNet-18 PAF (trained) + LLaMA2-7B (LoRA-finetuned) for reasoning
setting.training_data: R2R train trajectories; 5k MP3D goal-caption pairs for the SD LoRA; 30k quadruples for the PAF (Grounded-SAM pseudo masks); 250k+ generated R2R-Imagine images
setting.observation: egocentric RGB views from panoramas (36 discretized views per viewpoint), converted to captions plus imagined images and attention maps

numbers_note: RoboTHOR split and protocol are not specified. The ablation table (val-unseen) has w/o variants that were not added as separate entries. The +11.1% long-path SR gain on RoboTHOR is mentioned in the text without a table. The caption/abstract claims (+3.6% SR on R2R, +3.2% vs DUET-Imagine) are inconsistent with each other.
results: VISTA reaches 77.8 SR / 68.3 SPL on R2R val-unseen and 74.9 SR / 66.7 SPL on test-unseen, above DUET-Imagine (72.12 SR val) and PanoGen (74.2 SR val, 71.7 test). On RoboTHOR it reaches 43.1 SR / 28.8 SWPL versus ESC (38.1 / 22.2).
limitations: Depends on diffusion imagination fidelity; poor imagination or a misplaced attention mask misleads navigation.
Compute overhead of generation plus LLM reasoning; AIS thresholds are hand-tuned; simulation only.
Comparisons are partly non-uniform (baselines lack pretraining details); the RoboTHOR protocol and long-path analysis are under-specified.
